clue.text: Foreign secretary's valet — one of little substance

definitions.meaning: a manservant of Jack Straw, British Foreign Secretary 2001-06, would be Straw's man
a weak person or a feeble argument set up only to be knocked down

explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was the UK's Foreign Secretary when this ran, so his valet is his 'man'; the phrase also names a flimsy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw figure is a weak stand-in or a person without real influence, someone of no substance; the first reading is a pun on the politician's surname.

clue.text: Relocate to make progress

definitions.meaning: to shift house or change position
to advance, as in 'things are starting to happen'

explanation.definitionFit: To shift home is to change address, and a stalled project that starts to go forward is advancing; one verb covers both.

clue.text: The man too devious to be found out

indicators.note: devious means winding and indirect, so the three words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A man too cunning ever to be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found out' looks like 'exposed', but here it means simply 'out', away from home; 'devious' rearranges THE MAN TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out when a caller comes is absent from the house, unavailable to visitors.

clue.text: Look in marshland for vicious criminal

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside another here

parts.note: a fen is low wet marshy land, as in the East Anglian Fens
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Searching the bogs for a dangerous outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon commits a serious crime, and as an old adjective the word also meant cruel or wicked.

clue.text: Arrears setback for aviation engineers

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Arrears setback for aviation engineers'; the wordplay needs DEBT + SET reversed, so 'setback' must supply both SET and the reversal signal (likely 'set back' run together), a word doing two jobs.

clue.text: RAF boss is an idiot

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, giving the word air
a boss is a head, the person in charge

explanation.surface: A dig at the senior officer of the British air force.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a brainless, empty-headed person, a fool.

clue.text: He's got a cheek

parts.note: reads as a complaint about an impudent man, but a fellow has jaws, and the word also means a jaw or cheek

explanation.surface: Grumbling about someone's impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a man or fellow, and in an older sense the jaw or cheek, so such a fellow literally 'has a cheek'.

clue.text: Henry and Sally frequent it

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Aunt Sally is a British pub and fairground throwing game, so Sally suggests aunt

explanation.surface: Two people often visit a particular place.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a traditional British throwing game (and a byword for an easy target), so 'Sally' brings AUNT. 'frequent' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt a place is to visit it often, to be a regular there.

clue.text: Arrange to be enrolled as a monk

definitions.meaning: to sort or tidy into sequence

definitions.text: to be enrolled as a monk
definitions.meaning: to be placed in a religious order, as a brother is

explanation.definitionFit: To sort things neatly is to organise them; taken literally, a novice monk is placed within a religious order.

clue.text: Essential tincture first stored in medicine bottle

indicators.note: stored in means the letter is placed inside the bottle

parts.note: a vial is a small glass bottle for medicine

indicators.note: first asks for just the opening letter of the word tincture

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's note that tincture is kept in a phial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vital is indispensable, absolutely necessary.

clue.text: Unlikely dress for a temptress!

parts.note: a seductive woman is a siren, but this one-piece zip-up garment, worn in air-raid shelters, is hardly alluring

explanation.surface: A joke about what a seductress would never wear.
explanation.walkthrough: The garment is a baggy wartime one-piece made famous by Churchill; 'temptress' points to a siren, the seductive kind, so the joke is the mismatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece zipped boiler-suit garment, named after the air-raid warning, so dowdy that no seductress would choose it.

clue.text: Blink on seeing rubbish in French resort

indicators.note: in shows that one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
tat is cheap worthless stuff, junk

explanation.surface: Someone blinks at the sight of litter on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Nictating is the technical word for winking or blinking the eyelids.

clue.text: Typical measure taken by board is defensible

indicators.note: taken by means the measure is held within the board

parts.note: a board is a table, as in 'board and lodging'
an en is a printer's unit of type width, a typographical measure

explanation.surface: A standard measure approved by the directors can be justified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Typical' is a playful nod to type: EN is a printing measure, half an em. 'board' is a table, not a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position can be held or maintained against argument or attack.

clue.text: Copper can overtake dangerously

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a tin is a can, a metal container

explanation.surface: A police officer is able to pass other cars recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman and 'can' like 'is able to'; they are the element symbol and a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver who pulls into a gap just ahead of another vehicle after passing it does so rashly.

clue.text: Boy and man in Ely resolved to worship there

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: in tells us the man goes inside the rearranged letters
resolved here means broken down and reworked, so the letters of Ely are rearranged

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A boy and a man in Ely decide to attend church there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' looks like 'determined' but rearranges ELY into YEL, which holds CHAP: Y-CHAP-EL. Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel dedicated to the Virgin Mary inside a large church, often behind the high altar, used for prayer.

clue.text: Provoked by a banker in thoroughfare

indicators.note: in shows the river goes inside the road

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road
a banker is something with banks, a river; the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed by a financier on the main street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is the crossword's river (it has banks), here the Ouse, a river in Yorkshire and East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stirred up, excited or angered is to have one's feelings stoked.

clue.text: Not all passed a test for drugs

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An athlete only partly cleared a doping test.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the definition as 'for drugs'; 'for' is only a link joining wordplay to definition, so the definition is 'drugs', a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate someone is to calm them with tranquillisers, which is to dope them.

clue.text: Correspondence address for a master

parts.note: not a postal address but the form of words opening a letter to a man

explanation.surface: Asking where to send letters to a schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The conventional salutation opening a formal letter to a man is this two-word greeting.

clue.text: Pelt French cat for catching a bird

parts.note: to pelt is to stone, to throw missiles at
chat is the French word for cat

explanation.surface: Throwing things at a French cat to make it catch a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird of heath and scrub, named for its call like two pebbles knocked together.

clue.text: Gave in and gave out

definitions.meaning: produced, as a field produces a crop

explanation.definitionFit: To submit is to cede ground, and land that produces a harvest has produced it; one past tense covers both.

clue.text: Many develop slowly and pass on

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, standing for a large number
to evolve is to develop gradually

explanation.surface: Many people mature gradually before handing things on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives D because D is the Roman numeral for 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties that devolve are transferred or delegated to someone else.

clue.text: One woman sharp as a needle

parts.note: an ace is the one in a deck of cards
Rose is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman described as very quick-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp as a needle' sounds like praise of a woman's wit; it is the definition, a botanical word for needle-shaped leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for leaves that are narrow and pointed like pine needles.

clue.text: Relieved when everyone said yes?

parts.note: all means everyone
to say aye is to vote yes, so voted yes gives ayed

explanation.surface: Feeling relief when the whole group agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fears that are allayed are calmed or eased.

clue.text: Routine dress

definitions.meaning: the robe worn by a monk or nun, or riding clothes

explanation.definitionFit: A regular custom is a settled practice, and a nun's robe or a rider's outfit is clothing; one word for both.

clue.text: Living in Asian capital is initially joyless

indicators.note: read as is and joy with the less applying to their first letters: the capital loses the openings of is and joyless

parts.note: Beijing is the capital of China

explanation.surface: Life in the Chinese capital starts out cheerless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is initially joyless' asks the capital to lose the first letters of 'is' and 'joyless', I and J, which sit side by side in BEIJING.
explanation.definitionFit: Being is existence, the state of being alive.

clue.text: Six pupils get on in rural community

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
L is a learner, as on a British learner-driver's plate, so two pupils give two Ls
to age is to get on in years

explanation.surface: Half a dozen schoolchildren join a country settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plate that British learner drivers display; 'get on' means grow older.
explanation.definitionFit: A small settlement in the countryside, larger than a hamlet, smaller than a town.

clue.text: A question and answer by bachelor in Jordan

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A quiz session with a graduate in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqaba is the country's port city on the Red Sea gulf, its only outlet to the sea.

clue.text: Remarkable chap got the lady, it's said

indicators.note: it's said tells us the phrase is to be heard, not read

parts.note: got the lady means came to possess her: own her

explanation.surface: An impressive man won the woman, people say.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for an exceptional person or thing, one of a kind.

clue.text: Author makes ministerial pronouncement

indicators.note: a pronouncement is something spoken, so the word is to be heard

parts.note: ministerial in the church sense, like a clergyman: priestly

explanation.surface: A writer issues an official statement from government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ministerial' suggests government, but means clerical here; J. B. Priestley was the English author of 'An Inspector Calls'.
explanation.definitionFit: J. B. Priestley was an English novelist and playwright, so he is a writer.

clue.text: A man surrounded by tin of greyish hue

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the man inside the tin

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
he is a man, the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man encased in a grey metal can.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale as cinders, the colourless grey of a face drained by shock.

clue.text: Record nothing when trademark appears

parts.note: a log is a record, such as a ship's log
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Noting a blank whenever a brand mark shows up.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's emblem or design, used to identify its brand.

clue.text: Education wallah read them as ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the letters are put into another sequence

explanation.surface: A school official tells pupils to read what they were set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wallah' is Anglo-Indian slang for a person connected with a job. 'as ordered' looks like an instruction, but 'as' is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a school is the person in charge of education there; a 'wallah' is someone in a role.
